subject.title: feat(agents): add iteration budget for agent loop safety

question: Should `maxToolCallingRounds` remain a general agent setting that fails closed when Codex or another plugin harness is selected, or should it be scoped to the built-in embedded runtime until a harness-neutral capability exists?
rationale: The setting appears harness-agnostic in agent configuration, but enforcement exists only inside the built-in loop; Codex owns a separate app-server tool lifecycle, so automation cannot choose the permanent cross-harness contract safely.

options.title: Keep built-in-only enforcement
options.body: Retain the opt-in general setting and documented fail-closed behavior for non-built-in harnesses, then repair the boundary, test size, conflict, and exact-head proof blockers.

options.title: Scope under embedded runtime
options.body: Move the setting under the embedded OpenClaw configuration surface so unsupported plugin harnesses never inherit an apparently portable limit.

options.title: Pause for a harness capability
options.body: Defer the public setting until built-in and plugin harnesses expose one explicit tool-round-limit capability contract.

recommendation.title: Keep built-in-only enforcement
recommendation.body: Retain the opt-in general setting and documented fail-closed behavior for non-built-in harnesses, then repair the boundary, test size, conflict, and exact-head proof blockers.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal combines ownership of adjacent loop detection, agent-core loop work, and prior review of the canonical hard-budget direction.
